description:
FILED s543n (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-24) beside #4846 (the <> STDIN fallback).  PRE-EXISTING (base 617d66c8 = tree).

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 | PCL):
    my $s = "/tmp/x$$"; open(my $w, '>', $s) or die; print $w "s1\ns2\n"; close $w;
    open STDIN, "<", $s or die; @ARGV = ();
    my $a = <>; print "1 $a";                 # perl and PCL: 1 s1
    open STDIN, "<", "/dev/null" or die;
    my $b = <>; print "2 ", $b // "undef\n";  # perl: 2 s2      PCL: 2 undef
<> holds the STDIN stream it opened for the pass; re-opening STDIN dup2s the new file onto fd 0 and REBUILDS the CL
stream (%p-rebind-std), so the old stream object -- whose buffer holds "s2" -- is not what <> reads any more.  perl's
ARGV opened "-" on the same PerlIO, whose buffer survives the dup2.  Probe: the s543n worktree's
scratch/s543n/probes/pN1.pl rows 1-2.
frequency_reason: STDIN re-opened while `<>` is reading it (first pass from the subject, the reviewing session 2026-11-24)
subject: SILENT WRONG (rare): STDIN re-opened while `<>` is reading it -- perl's next `<>` reads the rest of what was already buffered from the old STDIN, PCL answers undef
triage_reason: a silent wrong of <> after STDIN is re-opened mid-pass: IN (rare)
